newsitem.title: UK: Britain's beloved "agony aunt" Marje Proops dies.
newsitem.headline: Britain's beloved "agony aunt" Marje Proops dies.

text.p: Britain's beloved "agony aunt" and journalist Marjorie Proops has died, her employers said on Sunday.
Proops, doyenne of newspaper advice columnists, kept her age a secret but was believed to be in her late 70s or early 80s, the Mirror Group of newspapers said.

"For those generations of working colleagues and millions upon millions of readers there will always be a special place in their hearts for Marje," David Montgomery, chief executive of the Mirror Group of newspapers, said.
Proops, whose advice column was a national fixture, died in a London hospital.

"She was a legend in journalism and will be sadly missed, not just by the Mirror and its readers, but by the country, who came to appreciate her warmth and generosity," said opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair.
Proops began working on the Daily Herald in 1945 as fashion editor but became an advice columnist for the Mirror in 1954.
By 1971 she had a staff of eight to handle the more than 50,000 letters that came to her every year.
